title: Parameterize a raw f-string SQL query
explanation: Replace string interpolation with a parameterized placeholder ('?' for sqlite3/DB-API, '%s' for psycopg2/MySQLdb) and pass the tainted value as a separate params tuple. The driver escapes the value itself, so it can never be interpreted as SQL syntax.

title: Parameterize a % -formatted SQL query with multiple values
explanation: Never build the SQL string with %-formatting before calling execute(). Keep the placeholders in the query literal and hand the values to execute() as a tuple so the DB-API driver parameterizes them.

title: Avoid shell=True with string concatenation
explanation: Replace os.system()/shell=True string concatenation with subprocess.run() given an argument list (shell=False). Passing arguments as a list means the OS invokes the binary directly instead of a shell, so metacharacters in target_dir (e.g. `; rm -rf /`) can't be interpreted. Also validate the resolved path stays within an allowed root.

title: Sanitize a filename passed to a shell pipeline
explanation: Validate the filename against an allowlist pattern before use, and switch to the argument-list form of subprocess with shell=False so the value is never parsed by a shell.

title: Resolve and confine a user-supplied path
vulnerable_code:
def read_file(base, filename):
    return open(base + filename).read()
explanation: Join the base directory and filename with os.path.join, resolve both with os.path.realpath to collapse '..' segments and symlinks, then verify the resolved target still starts with the resolved base directory before opening it.

title: Reject path traversal sequences in an upload handler
vulnerable_code:
def save_upload(upload_dir, filename, content):
    path = os.path.join(upload_dir, filename)
    with open(path, 'wb') as f:
        f.write(content)
fixed_code:
def save_upload(upload_dir, filename, content):
    safe_name = os.path.basename(filename)
    if safe_name != filename or safe_name in ('', '.', '..'):
        raise ValueError("invalid filename")
    path = os.path.join(upload_dir, safe_name)
    with open(path, 'wb') as f:
        f.write(content)
explanation: Strip any directory component from the user-supplied filename with os.path.basename and reject the request if the stripped name differs from the original (a sign it contained '/' or '..' segments).

title: Move a hardcoded password to an environment variable
explanation: Never commit credentials as string literals. Load the value from an environment variable (os.environ) or a secrets manager at runtime instead. Only replace this single assignment statement -- do not invent or reference any other function, variable, or import that isn't already present in the target file.

title: Remove a hardcoded API key constant
explanation: Read the API key from the environment at startup and raise immediately if it's missing, instead of embedding the live key in source control where it becomes permanently compromised. Only replace this constant's assignment -- do not invent or reference any other function, variable, or import that isn't already present in the target file.

title: Replace MD5 password hashing with a KDF
explanation: MD5/SHA1 are fast, unsalted, and trivially brute-forced for password storage. Use a slow, salted key-derivation function (pbkdf2_hmac, or better, bcrypt/argon2) with a per-password random salt, and store salt + derived key together.

title: Replace SHA1 integrity hash with SHA-256
explanation: SHA1 has known practical collision attacks. For integrity/digest purposes (not password storage) switch to SHA-256 or SHA-3, which have no known practical collisions.

title: Replace pickle with a safe format for untrusted data
explanation: pickle.loads can execute arbitrary code embedded in the payload during deserialization. If the data doesn't need to represent arbitrary Python objects, switch to json (or another data-only format). If pickle is unavoidable, cryptographically sign the payload and verify the signature before unpickling.

title: Verify an HMAC signature before unpickling
explanation: When pickle is required for trusted internal state (e.g. signed session cookies), append an HMAC signature computed with a server-side secret and verify it with a constant-time comparison before deserializing, so tampered payloads are rejected before pickle.loads ever runs.
